extracted.intended_audience: editors, proofreaders, typesetters, and authors using the University of Chicago Press / Chicago Manual of Style
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed editorial and typographic rules for preparing, setting, and proofreading text: capitalization, punctuation, hyphenation, numerals, tables, spacing, type styles, and indexing per the University of Chicago Press Manual of Style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of principal words in titles of publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization of principal words in titles of books, periodicals, pamphlets, parts of books, plays, poems, tracts, treatises, transactions, proceedings, series, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal words are capitalized (41); definite article not treated as part of newspaper/magazine titles (43); titles of publications usually italicized (60); when to roman-quote shorter items (80–82).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of italics vs. roman-quoting for titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Which kinds of titles are italicized and which are set in roman-quoted form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books, documents, treatises, series, pamphlets, periodicals, plays, separate volumes of poems, and many longer works set in italics (60); shorter works and subdivisions often roman-quoted (80–82); legal causes and proceedings italicized (63).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of the definite article in newspaper/magazine titles
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'The' is not to be treated as part of the title when applying capitalization rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat the article as part of the title for capitalization (43).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of proper nouns and proper names
rubrics_metrics.description: General rules for capitalizing proper names and forming possessives and derivatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper names capitalized (i, 5, 53); how to form possessive (113); verbs and adjectives derived from proper names may be lowercased (53); division of proper nouns to be avoided (218).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of titles and forms of address
rubrics_metrics.description: When academic, civil, military, nobility, honorary, and other titles are capitalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academic titles abbreviated (22); civil and military titles capitalization rules (21); 'President' and certain University of Chicago officers capitalization specifics (21, 49); titles not capitalized when spelled out in some contexts (22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of organizations, parties, religious denominations, and schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of organizations, political parties, religious denominations, philosophical/literary/artistic schools, and social organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names of organizations capitalized (ii); parties (9); religious denominations and sects (9); philosophical/literary/artistic schools (9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of geographic names, regions, and thoroughfares
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize numbered political divisions, regions or parts of the world, places, parks, squares, thoroughfares, and place-names with foreign treatment rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbered political divisions capitalization (7); regions/parts of world (5); parks, squares, thoroughfares capitalization (8); foreign place-names treatment guidance (59); states and territories abbreviations and treatment (100, 106).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of peoples, tribes, races, and epithets
rubrics_metrics.description: Names and epithets of peoples, races, and tribes are capitalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize names or epithets of peoples, races, and tribes (47).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization referring to Deity and sacred books
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names for the Supreme Being and pronouns referring to Deity; rules for capitalization of sacred books and Scripture passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supreme Being names and pronouns capitalized (24); names of sacred books capitalized (29); punctuation and abbreviation rules for Scripture passages (109, 134, 139).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of personifications and personified nature
rubrics_metrics.description: When personifications such as 'Nature' are capitalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personifications and personified Nature capitalization addressed (26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of scientific, zoological, and paleontological terms and species
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of capitals and italics in scientific names and terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitals for certain scientific terms (46); scientific and zoological species names use italics (46, 71); paleontological terms capitalization/italics (46, 71).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling out numbers at the beginning of sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers that commence a sentence should be spelled out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers commencing a sentence to be spelled out (96).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of numbers and numerals in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for when to spell out numbers versus set in figures, groups, punctuation, and use of dash for ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consecutive numbers treatment (159, 173); in connected groups treat alike (94); groups of six or more closely connected set in figures (94); numbers of less than three digits spelled out in ordinary reading matter (94); round numbers treatment (95); use comma after thousands (159); use comma to separate digits (154); use dash for 'to' connecting numbers (173).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerals at beginning of lines and headlines: spacing and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Spacing rules for Arabic and Roman numerals when they begin lines or appear in headlines and omission of period after numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spacing of Arabic and Roman numerals at beginning of lines and in headlines (271); omission of period after Roman numerals (124).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and formatting of percents and percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Percents to be expressed in figures; percentages in tables formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per cent to be expressed in figures and not treated as an abbreviation (94, 123); columns of percentages in tables may be set in distinctive type (241).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation general rules and placement with quotation marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules for punctuation, including placement relative to quotation marks and omission in classical references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punctuation rules cover 121–214; placing of period with quotation marks (126); omission of punctuation in classical references (237); punctuation marks printed in same type as preceding word (121).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation marks: usage and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use quotation marks, exceptions for reduced citations, and placement of various punctuation with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotation marks rules 74–91; not to be used with reduced citations except in specified exceptions (87, 75); placement of colon (136), comma (162), ellipsis (181), exclamation point (128), interrogation point (130), period (126); use of double and single quotes (91).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations: capitalization and integration
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat quotations within text, including capitalization of first word when connected to previous sentence and when to run quotes into text or reduce them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First word of quotation lowercased when connected to previous sentence (57); rules for reducing quotations and running them into text (74–91, 85).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commas in sequences and before conjunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of comma before 'and', 'or', 'nor' in sequences of three or more (series comma/Oxford comma) and use of comma in specific clause situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of comma before final 'and,' 'or,' and 'nor' in sequences of three or more (143); use of comma with parenthetical and adjectival phrases guidance (150, 152).

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicolon usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of semicolon to separate distinct clauses in enumerations and to mark divisions within sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semicolon separates two or more distinct clauses in enumerations; illustrated vs comma use; placement with quotation marks and use in enumerations and Scripture references containing chapters (137–40).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dashes and their functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions of dash: indicating pause, transition, summarizing clauses, and spacing/types (two-em, three-em).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dash for pause (166), transition (166), summarizing clauses (170); definitions and illustrations of two-em and three-em dashes and quads (261).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parentheses and brackets
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for using parentheses for parenthetical clauses, parentheses with subsection indicators, and use of brackets within parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for parentheses 176–77; use for parenthetical clauses (177); parentheses in connection with figures/letters for subsections (176); within parentheses use brackets (178).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parenthetical clauses punctuation options
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use commas, dashes, or parentheses for parenthetical clauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of commas with parenthetical clauses (150), use of dashes (167, 169), and use of parentheses (177).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation and treatment of prefixes/compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for hyphenating prefixes and compounds (co-, non-, un-, re-, pre-, post-, self-, sub-, super-, quasi-, semi-, tri-, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of compound prefixes and guidance: 'co-','pre-','re-' treatment (203); 'non-','un-','a-' compounds (205); 'self-' compounds (198); 'sub-','super-','quasi-','semi-' etc. (197–209); prefix/suffix not complete in itself indicated by hyphen (212).

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission and use of apostrophe for omitted letters/figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of apostrophe to indicate omission of figures or letters in the middle of a word and rules for omission of ellipsis/periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use apostrophe for omission of figures/letters in middle of word (163); omission of period after headlines, Roman numerals, and certain abbreviations (125, 124, 123); use of brackets to indicate omitted words (178); omission of ellipsis rules (180).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of plurals and plurals of abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: How to form plurals of ordinary nouns, numerals, and abbreviations in literary references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formation of plurals (165); plurals of abbreviations in literary references guidance (no); plurals of numerals formation (165); of nouns not divisible if singular not divisible (228).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possessive case formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for forming the possessive case, including for proper names ending in sibilants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possessive case formation rules (113, 164); possessives of proper names ending in sibilant guidance (113).

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of punctuation after signatures and headings
rubrics_metrics.description: When to omit comma or period after signatures, running heads, side-heads, and similar elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of comma after signatures etc. (161); omission of period after headlines, running-heads, side-heads, and superscriptions (125).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling conventions and lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and lists for spelling words with multiple forms and special items (ages, centuries, months, names, decades, company abbreviations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spelling rules 92–120; list of words with more than one spelling (119); spelling of ages (99), centuries (100), months (102), 'Company' and 'Brothers' in firm names (107), decades (101), Egyptian dynasties (100), etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations: when to use periods and when to omit
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use and omission of periods after abbreviations and special abbreviations lists (Bible versions, states, centuries, typesetting abbreviations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit period after initials of publication titles and Roman numerals (123, 124); lists of abbreviations for Old and New Testament books and versions (109); lists for states and territories (106); 'Vol., chap., p.' usage in literary references (237).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and tabular work rules
rubrics_metrics.description: How to set open and ruled tables, headlines, box-heads, reading matter, two-column vs multi-column tables, specimen tables, and use of distinctive type for totals/percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for tables 241–50: open tables headlines and how to set (241–242); two-column tables set as open (248); more-than-two columns as ruled (248); box-heads for ruled tables (242); specimen tables (250); reading-matter placement in ruled/open tables (245–246).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of en-dash for consecutive pages and ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Use en-dash/spacing to indicate ranges (consecutive pages, numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of en-dash between consecutive pages (158 cf. 173); dash used for 'to' connecting numbers (173).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing rules in composition and typography
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for spacing in foundry, linotype, monotype composition, spacing of divisional signs, figure columns, headlines, metric and monetary symbols, and standard space sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spacing rules 258–73: spacing explained, standard (262); effect on etymological divisions (221); spacing of divisional signs (269); spacing of figure columns in tables (245); spacing of numerals at beginning of paragraphs/headlines (271); thin/thick/wide spacing definitions and where to avoid (261, 265).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type styles, sizes, and specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation and specimens of type styles (body types, italics, small caps, bolds, gothic, etc.) and size samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Styles of type and specimens 253–57 and throughout specimen pages; samples of sizes and styles for body type and display (252–257); small pica, pica, quads, three-em/quads defined (252, 261).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small caps: definition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of small caps, how indicated, and when to use them in headings and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small caps defined and how indicated (257); use in tabular work (242, 249) and in headings (279); use for sectional headings and labels (51).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph styles, indentation, and plain paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of paragraph types, styles, indention rules for plain and regular paragraphs and for quoted prose indention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain paragraph defined and illustrated (284); indention rules (274); paragraph styles 276; first lines of quoted prose begin with quotation marks (89); paragraph mark spacing (269).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading marks and hints to proofreaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Hints for proofreaders and the standard marks to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints to proofreaders and marks described (pp. 117–19; p. 123).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and descriptions of proofs and proof terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions for page-proof, plate-proof, proofs, revise, and related typographical terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page-proof defined (286); plate-proof defined (287); proofs description 285–89; 'revise' defined (289).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing rules for names and special characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of particles (van, von), O', umlauted names, and indexing of forms like 'St.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for particles in French/Dutch/German names capitalization and indexing (3, 240); rule for 'Van','Von' (3, 240); umlaut indexing (240); 'St.' indexing rule (240); rule for O' in indexing (240).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of superior figures and sequence of footnote indices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of superior (superscript) figures for footnote indices and sequencing of indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Superior figures for reference indices (232, 234); sequences of footnote indices guidance (232).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of abbreviations for units, symbols, and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: How to abbreviate units of measurement, how to space metric and monetary symbols, and when to spell out symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units of measurement abbreviations and lower-case initial (55); metric symbols spacing (269); monetary symbols spacing (270); treatment of chemical symbols and measurement symbols (123).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for headlines, side-heads, and running-heads
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and setting hints for headlines, running-heads, side-heads, and their punctuation conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running-heads defined and omission of period after them (283, 125); side-heads defined, omission of period, and use of dash and lower-case in them (280, 172, 56); spacing and headline spacing rules (271).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of literary references and subdivisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Punctuation, abbreviation, and capitalization rules for literary references and for subdivisions within references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literary references punctuation and lists of words to abbreviate (237, 239); subdivisions in literary references use lower-case (54 cf. no, 237); letters indicating subdivisions set in italics (66); use of parentheses with subdivisions (66).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of quotation marks and special treatment for words called out
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use quotation marks for unusual words, words accompanied by definitions, and technical terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quotation marks for unusual or attention-directing words (76–79); use quotation marks for words or phrases accompanied by their definition (76); use quotes for technical words/phrases as needed (77).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for setting two-column vs multi-column tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-column tables to be set as open; tables of more than two columns to be set as ruled; headlines and box-head rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-column tables set as open (248); tables of more than two columns set as ruled (248); open-table headlines and box-head guidance (241–242).
